texts.li: {A_nameDef} has been in bed with {ILLNESS} for two days and isn't getting better on broth and rest. The colony is down to its last few doses of medicine, and nobody knows what the next month will bring.\n\nThe council has to decide whether to spend some of it on {A_nameDef} now.

[lowtech] The herb shelf is nearly bare: a few bundles of healroot tied with string, and nothing more until the next harvest. {A_nameDef} is down with {ILLNESS} and coughing through the nights. Whoever tends {A_objective} wants to know whether the last bundles go to {A_nameDef} or stay on the shelf.

[!lowtech] There are a few kits of medicine left in the stores, and {A_nameDef} has {ILLNESS}. It isn't dangerous yet. The doctor would like to treat it properly anyway, and the quartermaster would like to know what happens when someone is shot next week.

li.label: Treat {A_nameDef} with the medicine
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} treated {A_nameDef} with one of the last doses. The fever broke that night, and {A_nameDef} is sitting up and complaining about the food, which is a good sign.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {B_nameDef} boiled the last of the healroot into a bitter tea and made {A_nameDef} drink every drop. By morning {A_nameDef} was sleeping easier, and the shelf was bare.
[b:past:healer] {B_nameDef} knew exactly how much to use and not a pinch more. {A_nameDef} is mending, and there's still a dose or two left on the shelf.
[winter] {B_nameDef} treated {A_nameDef} by the stove with one of the last doses. Outside the snow came down, and inside {A_nameDef} finally slept through the night.

li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} used one of the last doses on {A_nameDef}, and it didn't seem to touch the {ILLNESS}. The medicine is gone and {A_nameDef} is no better, though {B_nameDef} says these things take time.

li.label: Keep the medicine; rest and broth instead
li.outcome: The medicine stays on the shelf. {A_nameDef} has a bed by the stove, broth three times a day and orders not to lift anything. {A_nameDef} is following the orders and not enjoying them.

outcomes.li: [trait:Ascetic] The medicine stays on the shelf, and {A_nameDef} says that's how it should be. A bed, broth and time: {A_pronoun} has got over worse with less.
[colony:Thrifty] The colony keeps what it has, as usual. {A_nameDef} got broth, a blanket and a long speech about the winters ahead.

li.label: Send a forager out for wild herbs
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} came back from the scrub at dusk with an apron full of leaves and roots, and boiled them into a tea for {A_nameDef}. It smelled like a ditch. {A_nameDef} is breathing easier.

outcomes.li: [land:desert] {B_nameDef} walked half a day to a dry gully where the bitter shrubs grow, and came back with enough for a week of tea. {A_nameDef} pulls a face at every cup and is getting better anyway.
[land:jungle|land:swamp] {B_nameDef} waded out to the wet ground and came back muddy to the thighs with a sack of leaves. Boiled down, they made {A_nameDef} sweat out the worst of the {ILLNESS}.
[b:skill:Plants] {B_nameDef} knew exactly where to look, and was back before noon. {A_nameDef} has been drinking the tea all afternoon and says it tastes like grass, which it is.

li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} searched until dark and came back with the wrong leaves, or with nothing. {A_nameDef} is still in bed with {ILLNESS}, and {B_nameDef} has a new respect for herb-gatherers.

riskOutcomes.li: [winter] {B_nameDef} dug through the snow all afternoon looking for anything green, and came back with frozen fingers and nothing else. {A_nameDef} is no better.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has {ILLNESS} and shares a room with others, and they've started sleeping with their blankets over their faces. Someone suggested moving {A_nameDef} out until it passes, to the storeroom or a bed of {A_possessive} own.\n\n{A_nameDef} heard about the suggestion before the council did, and didn't take it well.

[ail:Typhus|ail:Tuberculosis] Everyone knows what {ILLNESS} can do among people who sleep side by side. {A_nameDef} has it. The others want {A_objective} out of the shared room tonight, and {A_nameDef}, who can barely sit up, wants to know if {A_pronoun} is being thrown out.
[child] {A_nameDef} has {ILLNESS}, and the grown-ups want {A_objective} kept away from the other children until it passes. {A_nameDef} wants to know why nobody will play with {A_objective}.

li.label: Move {A_nameDef} to a bed apart
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sleeps on a cot in a room of {A_possessive} own until the {ILLNESS} passes. People talk to {A_objective} through the door and leave food on the step. It works, and {A_nameDef} hates it.

outcomes.li: [child] {A_nameDef} has a bed apart until the {ILLNESS} is gone. The other children leave drawings outside the door, and {A_nameDef} has started drawing back.
[lowtech] They hung a hide across the corner of the storeroom and made {A_nameDef} a bed behind it. Meals come on a board pushed under the hide, and {A_nameDef} counts the days.

li.label: Keep {A_nameDef} where {A_pronoun} is
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} stays in {A_possessive} own bed, with the window open and a bucket of water by the door for washing hands. The others are being very polite about it.

outcomes.li: [colony:Merciful] This colony doesn't put its sick out of the room, and the council said so. {A_nameDef} stays. The others have moved their beds a foot further away.

li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} stays where {A_pronoun} is. Two of the others took their bedding out to the hall rather than share the room, and made sure everyone saw them do it.

li.label: Have someone nurse {A_nameDef} apart from the rest
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} moved {A_nameDef} into a room apart and moved in with {A_objective}, with a basin, clean cloths and a chair to sleep in. The rest of the colony brings food to the door, and {A_nameDef} isn't alone with it.

outcomes.li: [b:trait:Kind] {B_nameDef} sat up with {A_nameDef} every night, reading aloud and changing the cloths. {A_nameDef} says it was the reading that helped most.
[b:past:healer] {B_nameDef} has nursed people through worse, and set up the room in an hour and ran it like an infirmary. {A_nameDef} is mending.

li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} nursed {A_nameDef} apart from the rest, night and day. {A_nameDef} is mending. {B_nameDef} looks like the one who has been ill.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has {ILLNESS} and is still at the stove, sniffing over the pot and wiping {A_possessive} nose on {A_possessive} sleeve between stirs. {A_nameDef} says the cooking won't do itself, which is true. Several people have stopped eating what comes out of the kitchen, which is also true.

[ail:StomachBug] {A_nameDef} has a stomach bug and won't stay out of the kitchen. "I wash my hands," {A_nameDef} says, between trips to the latrine. The others would like the council to decide who cooks until it passes.

{A_nameDef} is the colony's cook and has {ILLNESS}. Somebody saw {A_objective} cough into the bread dough this morning, and by supper the story had grown. {A_nameDef} says it was the flour, not the dough, and wants to keep cooking.

li.label: Out of the kitchen; someone else cooks until it passes
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} has been sent to bed and {B_nameDef} is at the stove. The meals are plainer. {A_nameDef} comes to the kitchen door every hour to say what {B_nameDef} is doing wrong.

outcomes.li: [b:skill:Cooking] {B_nameDef} took over the kitchen and, to {A_nameDef}'s quiet horror, the meals are just as good. {A_nameDef} has started getting better faster.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} cook, with clean hands and a cloth over the face
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} cooks with a cloth tied over {A_possessive} nose and mouth and scrubs {A_possessive} hands raw between every dish. The food is as good as ever. Some people eat it anyway and some people eat it slowly.

li.label: Cold suppers for a few days
li.outcome: The stove is cold and {A_nameDef} is in bed. Supper is bread, cold meat and whatever is in the jars, and it will be until the cook is well.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] Supper is flatbread, smoked meat and pickled roots out of the crock, eaten cold. {A_nameDef} is in bed, and the colony has learned what it thinks of pickled roots.
[winter] Cold suppers in the middle of winter. People eat standing round the hearth, and {A_nameDef} is under orders to rest until the stove can be lit again.

texts.li: {B_nameDef} has a cure for {ILLNESS} that {B_possessive} grandmother swore by: a poultice of onions and lard, bound to the chest overnight and changed at dawn. {A_nameDef} can already smell it from across the room. {B_nameDef} has asked the council to let {B_objective} try, and whoever does the colony's doctoring has asked the council not to.

{B_nameDef} has been telling anyone who will listen that {A_nameDef}'s {ILLNESS} wants a steam tent: a blanket, a basin of boiling water with pine needles in it, and {A_nameDef}'s head under the blanket for as long as {A_pronoun} can stand it. {B_nameDef} has seen it work a hundred times. Nobody else here has seen it work once.

[lowtech] {B_nameDef} wants to treat {A_nameDef}'s {ILLNESS} the old way: garlic and mustard seed ground into a paste, wrapped in cloth, and worn against the skin for three days. {B_nameDef}'s mother did it, and her mother. The colony's healer would rather stick to the herbs on the shelf.

li.label: Let {B_nameDef} try the old remedy
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} made up the remedy and saw to it all night. By morning {A_nameDef} was breathing easier and smelled terrible, and {B_nameDef} has been very gracious about being right.

outcomes.li: {B_nameDef} made it up exactly as {B_pronoun} was taught as a child, humming the whole time. {A_nameDef} feels better and has promised never to mention the smell.
[winter] Wrapped in the remedy by the stove, with the wind banging at the shutters, {A_nameDef} slept the night through. {B_nameDef} sat up beside {A_objective} the whole night.

li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} tried the remedy and it did nothing but smell. {A_nameDef} is just as ill and has been asked to eat supper at the end of the table.

li.label: Medicine from the stores, and no remedy
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} was treated with medicine from the stores and is mending. {B_nameDef} has told several people, at length, what {B_pronoun} would have done instead.

li.label: Both: the remedy at night, the doctor by day
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} sees to the remedy at night and the colony's doctor checks on {A_nameDef} by day, and the two of them pass each other at the door without speaking. {A_nameDef} is getting better, and nobody can say which of them to thank.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, one of the {FACTION} visitors, has {THEIRILLNESS} and asked {A_nameDef} at the gate whether the colony could spare any medicine. The colony has only a few doses left, and {X_nameDef}'s people will be gone in a day either way.

[theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has {THEIRILLNESS} and came to {A_nameDef} with {X_possessive} hat in {X_possessive} hands, asking for whatever the colony's healer could spare. There isn't much to spare.

[x:old] {X_nameDef} is the oldest of the {FACTION} party and has {THEIRILLNESS}. The others in the party asked {A_nameDef} for medicine on {X_possessive} behalf, because {X_nameDef} is too proud to ask.

li.label: Give {X_nameDef} a dose
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} treated {X_nameDef} with one of the colony's last doses. The {FACTION} visitors will remember it, and {X_nameDef} shook {A_nameDef}'s hand twice before leaving.

outcomes.li: [theirLowtech] {A_nameDef} gave {X_nameDef} a dose and showed {X_objective} how to take the rest of the course. {X_nameDef} bowed, which {FACTION} people don't do lightly.

li.label: Have {A_nameDef} look at {X_objective}, but keep the medicine
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} examined {X_nameDef}, told {X_objective} to rest and drink, and wrapped {X_objective} in a warm blanket for the road. The medicine stayed on the shelf. {X_nameDef} was polite about it.

li.label: We can't spare anything
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} told {X_nameDef} the colony has nothing to spare. {X_nameDef} nodded, went back to the other visitors, and coughed the rest of the evening where everyone could hear.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, traveling with the {FACTION} party, says {X_pronoun} has seen {ILLNESS} before and knows the cure: {A_nameDef} sits in the creek up to the neck at dawn, then is wrapped in hot blankets and fed raw garlic until the sickness sweats out.\n\n{A_nameDef} is willing to try almost anything. Whoever does the colony's doctoring is not.

{X_nameDef} of {FACTION} watched {A_nameDef} cough through supper, then went to {X_possessive} pack and came back with a small pot of black paste. It goes on the soles of the feet, {X_nameDef} says, under wool socks, for three nights. It cured {X_possessive} brother of the same {ILLNESS}, and {X_possessive} brother is still alive, so there.

[theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} wants to burn bitter herbs over {A_nameDef}'s bed and sing over {A_objective} through the night, the way {FACTION} healers do for {ILLNESS}. {X_nameDef} asks nothing for it except a seat by the fire and a share of the soup.

[theirHightech] {X_nameDef} has a pouch of gray pills with no label and swears by them for {ILLNESS}: two at dawn, two at dusk, nothing to eat in between. {X_nameDef} got them from a ship's doctor, or someone who said they were one.

li.label: Let {X_nameDef} try the cure
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} did everything {X_nameDef} said, every part of it, with the colony watching from a polite distance. The next morning the {ILLNESS} had eased. Nobody can say why, and {X_nameDef} doesn't seem to need them to.

outcomes.li: [theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} sang over {A_nameDef} all night in a language nobody here knows, and the room filled with bitter smoke. By morning {A_nameDef} was sitting up and asking for breakfast.
[cold|winter] The creek was half ice. {A_nameDef} went in to the neck anyway, came out blue, and was wrapped in every blanket in the colony. The fever broke before noon.

li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} went through every step of {X_nameDef}'s cure, and the {ILLNESS} didn't notice. {X_nameDef} says it takes longer in some people. The colony has a new story to tell about {A_nameDef}.

riskOutcomes.li: [theirHightech] The gray pills turned out to taste of chalk, because they were chalk. {A_nameDef} took all of them anyway and is no better.

li.label: Let {X_nameDef} try it, with our doctor watching
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} stood at {X_nameDef}'s elbow through the whole cure, asking what each part was for and writing the answers down. {A_nameDef} is somewhat better, and {B_nameDef} knows more than {B_pronoun} did.

outcomes.li: [b:skill:Medicine] {B_nameDef} and {X_nameDef} argued over every step and agreed on about half of them. {A_nameDef} got the half they agreed on and is mending.

li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} watched every step of the cure. It didn't work, but {B_nameDef} came away with a list of things not to try, which {B_pronoun} says is the more useful kind of list.

li.label: Thank {X_nameDef}, and decline
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} thanked {X_nameDef} and said no. {X_nameDef} shrugged and put the cure away, and {A_nameDef} has been wondering about it ever since.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} walked over from the {FACTION} camp this morning with a child on {X_possessive} hip, flushed with fever and too tired to lift its head. Their healer died on the road, {X_nameDef} says, and the fever has gone through three of them already.\n\n{X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} for medicine, or for someone who knows what to do with it.

[theirLowtech] The smoke from the {FACTION} camp has been thin for two days, and today {X_nameDef} came to the gate to say why: half of them are down with a fever, and their herbs ran out on the road. {X_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef}, plainly, for help.

[winter] The {FACTION} camp has been coughing all week; the colony can hear it on still nights. This morning {X_nameDef} came across the snow to ask {A_nameDef} whether the colony could spare medicine, food, or a healer for a day.

li.label: Send them medicine
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} carried two doses of medicine over to the camp and stayed to show them how to use it. Within days the coughing at night had quieted, and {X_nameDef} sent back a basket of something dried and spiced as thanks.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {A_nameDef} took two bundles of healroot over to the camp and showed them how to steep it. By the end of the week their fire was burning high again.

li.label: Send our doctor to tend them
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} spent two days at the {FACTION} camp, going from bedroll to bedroll with a basin and a bag. The fever is passing there now. {B_nameDef} came home hoarse, tired and in demand.

outcomes.li: [b:past:healer] {B_nameDef} has worked in sick tents before and ran the camp like one: the sick on one side, the well on the other, boiled water for everything. The fever burned out in three days.
[b:trait:Kind] {B_nameDef} sat with the feverish child through the worst night and held its hand until morning. The whole camp knows {B_possessive} name now.

li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} did what {B_pronoun} could at the camp, which wasn't much without medicine. The fever ran its course anyway. The {FACTION} people thanked {B_nameDef} for trying, and meant it.

li.label: Food and blankets, not medicine
li.outcome: The colony sent over a sack of food and every spare blanket. The sick at the camp are warm and fed, and getting better slowly, the way people do.

li.label: Keep our distance
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} told {X_nameDef} the colony can't risk the fever coming inside its walls. {X_nameDef} went back to the camp without a word, and the coughing goes on at night.

ColonyCouncil.DilemmaDef.label: an empty pot at the camp

texts.li: {X_nameDef} came up from the {FACTION} camp this evening and waited just outside the firelight until {A_nameDef} noticed {X_objective}. The hunting has been bad all week, {X_nameDef} said, and the camp's last sack of meal ran out yesterday. They'll pay it back when they can. {X_nameDef} didn't say when that would be.
[winter] The snow has driven the game off, and the {FACTION} camp has been living on boiled roots and hope. {X_nameDef} came to {A_nameDef} to ask for food, and looked thinner than when they arrived.

[theirLowtech] {X_nameDef} came to the colony with an empty clay pot under {X_possessive} arm and set it down in front of {A_nameDef} without a word. Among {FACTION} people, {X_nameDef} explained afterward, that is how a hungry camp asks.

li.label: Fill their pot
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sent {X_nameDef} back to the camp with enough food for a week. That evening the camp's fire burned high, and there was singing.

outcomes.li: [colony:Generous] It's what this colony does, and everyone knew it before the council said so. {X_nameDef} went back with a full pot and a sack besides.

li.label: Have our best tracker show their hunters the game
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} took two of their hunters out before dawn and showed them the trails and the watering places. They came back at dusk carrying a carcass between them, and the camp ate well.

outcomes.li: [land:desert] {B_nameDef} took their hunters to the one spring for a day's walk, where the animals come at dusk. They waited in the rocks until dark and came home with meat.
[land:tundra|land:boreal] {B_nameDef} showed their hunters how to read the tracks in the crust of the snow and where the herds shelter from the wind. The camp ate meat that night.

li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} walked their hunters all over the land for a day and they didn't see so much as a rabbit. They came back empty-handed but on better terms.

li.label: Food for work: they can earn it
li.outcome: The camp's people spent two days chopping and stacking wood for the colony, and went home each evening with full sacks. Everyone agrees it was a fair trade, and nobody quite says thank you.

li.label: We have nothing to spare
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} told {X_nameDef} the colony has nothing to spare. {X_nameDef} took the answer back to the camp. The fire there was small that night.

ColonyCouncil.DilemmaDef.label: a child missing from the camp

texts.li: A child from the {FACTION} camp wandered off after a goat this afternoon and hasn't come back. {X_nameDef} is going from fire to fire with a torch, calling the child's name, and has asked {A_nameDef} for searchers: people who know the land.

[winter] A child from the {FACTION} camp went out to collect firewood at noon and hasn't come back, and it will be dark and bitterly cold in a few hours. {X_nameDef} came running to the colony to ask for every pair of eyes it can spare.

[land:swamp|land:jungle] A child from the {FACTION} camp followed a bird into the thick growth past the camp and didn't come out. {X_nameDef} has been shouting into the green since midday, and came to {A_nameDef} for help.

li.label: Send our best tracker to search
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} followed small footprints and goat droppings until well after dark, and found the child asleep in a hollow with the goat curled up beside it. {B_nameDef} carried the child back to the camp, and {X_nameDef} wept.

outcomes.li: [winter] {B_nameDef} found the child in the snow under a fallen tree, cold and frightened and unharmed, and brought them back wrapped in {B_possessive} own coat.
[b:skill:Animals] {B_nameDef} tracked the goat rather than the child, guessing correctly that the child would be wherever the goat was. Both were back by moonrise.

li.reason: Needs someone who can read tracks (Animals 4 or more)

li.label: the search for the lost child

li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} searched all night with the camp's people. Near dawn one of their own found the child under a hedge, cold and sulking and fine. {B_nameDef} came home stiff and tired, and the camp was grateful for the help.

li.label: the search for the lost child
Lend them lights and let them search
li.outcome: The colony lent the camp every lamp and torch it could spare. They searched by those lights and found the child before midnight, curled up asleep against the goat.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] The colony handed over a bundle of pitch torches. Their light bobbed among the trees for hours before a shout went up: the child was found, asleep against the goat.

li.label: Keep the gate lit and the bell ringing all night
li.outcome: The colony kept its gate lit and someone rang the bell every hour until dawn. Just before first light the child came walking out of the dark toward the sound, leading the goat. Nobody at the colony slept much.

lines.li: Can you hear anything out there?

li.label: It's their child and their search
li.outcome: The colony stayed behind its walls and watched the torches move about in the dark. The camp's own people found the child at dawn, asleep against the goat. {X_nameDef} hasn't spoken to anyone at the colony since.

texts.li: The council met while {A_nameDef} was out at work and decided things {A_nameDef} has opinions about. {A_nameDef} heard about it over breakfast from three different people, each of whom told it differently.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants it all opened up again, with {A_objective} in the room this time.

[doubtful|bitter] {A_nameDef} missed the last council meeting and doesn't think {A_pronoun} missed much. The council decides what it likes, in {A_possessive} view, and the meetings are for show. Now {A_nameDef} says the meeting proved {A_objective} right, and wants the council to answer for it.

[night|evening] {A_nameDef} came back from the far fields long after dark to find the meeting over and the chairs stacked. Decisions were made. {A_nameDef} was not consulted, and has asked the council, coldly, whether this is how it will be from now on.

li.label: Hear {A_nameDef} out at the next meeting
li.outcome: The council went over the whole thing again with {A_nameDef} in the room. Nothing much changed, but {A_nameDef} had {A_possessive} say, and the others had to sit through it twice.

li.label: What was decided stands
li.outcome: The council told {A_nameDef} the decisions stand. {A_nameDef} said nothing and left the room, and has been short with everyone since.

outcomes.li: [colony:Hardworking] The council said that in a colony this busy, meetings happen when they happen. {A_nameDef} said that in that case {A_pronoun} would stop working late. Nobody can tell if {A_pronoun} meant it.

li.label: From now on, meetings wait for those at work
li.outcome: The council decided that from now on no meeting starts until everyone is in from work. {A_nameDef} was pleased. Supper on meeting nights is later, and the cook has things to say about that.

li.label: Have a good talker tell {A_nameDef} the whole of it
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} sat down with {A_nameDef} that evening and went through everything the meeting had said, who argued for what and why it came out the way it did. {A_nameDef} still doesn't agree with all of it, but understands it.

outcomes.li: [b:office:Speaker] The speaker went over the whole meeting with {A_nameDef} point by point, as the chair is supposed to. {A_nameDef} left satisfied, if not happy.

li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} tried to explain the meeting to {A_nameDef} and only made it sound worse. They ended up arguing about it in the yard, and {A_nameDef} is angrier than before.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} came to the council looking worn to the bone and asked for a few days to do nothing at all. The timing could hardly be worse, and {A_nameDef} knows it. {A_nameDef} asked anyway.

[afterraid] The walls are still being patched after the raid, and {A_nameDef} has asked for two days off. {A_nameDef} has been on every shift since the attack and looks it: gray in the face, jumpy, sleeping in {A_possessive} boots. The council can spare {A_objective}, or it can't.

[fall] The harvest is coming in, every hand is in the fields, and {A_nameDef} has asked for a few days off. Not later. Now. {A_nameDef} has worked harder than most this season, and this week has started to come apart: snapping at people, forgetting things, staring at nothing over supper.

li.label: Give {A_nameDef} the days
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} has a few days off, by order of the council. {A_nameDef} slept most of the first one, sat by the water for the second, and on the third came to supper and laughed at something.

outcomes.li: [afterraid] The walls can wait two days, the council decided. {A_nameDef} slept through the first of them and woke up looking ten years younger.
[fall] The others are bringing in the harvest without {A_nameDef}, and a few of them are making a point of how hard it is. {A_nameDef} is sleeping through it.

li.label: Lighter work until the rush is over
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is on light work for now: mending, sorting, jobs done sitting down. It isn't the rest {A_pronoun} asked for, and it isn't nothing.

li.label: Ask {A_nameDef} to hold on until the rush is over
li.outcome: The council asked {A_nameDef} to hold on until the worst is over. {A_nameDef} nodded and went back to work, and hasn't said much to anyone since.
li.riskOutcome: The council asked {A_nameDef} to hold on until the rush is over. {A_nameDef} went back to work, and an hour later put down {A_possessive} tools and walked away from the colony without a word, and didn't come back until dark.

li.label: Everyone takes a half day, in turn
li.outcome: The council gave everyone a half day off in turn until the rush is over, {A_nameDef} first. The work goes slower. People are smiling at supper again.

texts.li: It started small: a muddy floor, a seat taken at supper, a joke that didn't land. Between {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} it hasn't stayed small. This week they stopped speaking except through other people, and the other people are tired of carrying messages.\n\nThe council has been asked to do something before it turns into a real feud.

{B_nameDef} keeps a list of everything {A_nameDef} does wrong, and has started reading from it at meals. {A_nameDef} has started a list of {A_possessive} own. Each says the other started it, and both are probably right.

[winter] Shut in together all winter, {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} have worn each other down to the nerve. Today it was who left the door open; yesterday, whose turn it was at the woodpile. The rest of the colony has asked the council to sort them out before spring.

li.label: Sit them down and make them talk it out
li.outcome: The council sat {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} down at the same table with a mediator between them and nothing else to do until they were done. It took most of the evening. They came out talking to each other, carefully.

li.reason: Needs someone to keep the peace between them (Social 6 or more)

li.riskOutcome: The council sat them down to talk it out. They talked it out, all of it, at the top of their voices, and left by different doors.

li.label: Separate chores, separate tables
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} now do different jobs at different hours and eat at opposite ends of the table. It's quieter. A few other people had their chores moved to make it work.

li.label: One week, one job, together
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} spent a week on the same job, side by side, by order of the council. On the fourth day one of them made a joke and the other laughed before remembering not to.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} spent a week on the same job and finished it in silence. Neither will say a word about the other now, good or bad.

li.label: Leave them to it
li.outcome: The council stayed out of it. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} are still at it, and the people who eat between them have started eating somewhere else.
li.riskOutcome: The council stayed out of it, and {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} took that to mean nobody would stop them. It's a proper feud now.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has done more than {A_possessive} share of every job the colony has. This morning {A_pronoun} came to the council and asked, calmly, to stop. Not to leave: to sit in the sun, mend things when {A_pronoun} feels like it, and let younger people like {B_nameDef} do the heavy work.\n\nThe colony isn't large enough to lose a pair of hands without feeling it.

{A_nameDef} had to sit down halfway up the stairs yesterday, and today asked the council for something {A_pronoun} has never asked for before: to be let off the heavy work for good. {A_nameDef} has been carrying, hauling and digging since before {B_nameDef} was born.

[winter] The cold has got into {A_nameDef}'s hands this winter, and {A_pronoun} can't close them around a tool handle in the mornings. {A_nameDef} wants to put down the tools and spend what's left of the winter by the fire, teaching {B_nameDef} and the others what {A_pronoun} knows.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} rest; {A_pronoun} has earned it
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} has put down the heavy work, by leave of the council. {A_nameDef} sits in the sun most mornings, mends things in the afternoons and has opinions about everything the young ones do.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {A_nameDef} has taken the bench by the door as {A_possessive} own. From there {A_pronoun} whittles, shells beans and tells the children which of the adults to ignore.
[colony:Traditional] This colony looks after its old ones, and the council said so at supper so everyone would hear. {A_nameDef} wiped {A_possessive} eyes and blamed the smoke.

li.label: Ask {A_nameDef} to teach {B_nameDef} instead
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} has put down the heavy work and picked up a student. {B_nameDef} follows {A_objective} about all day with questions, and {A_nameDef} answers most of them.

outcomes.li: [trait:Abrasive] {A_nameDef} has taken {B_nameDef} on as a student and is a terrible teacher: impatient, rude and right about everything. {B_nameDef} is learning fast, mostly out of spite.

li.label: Lighter work: mending and minding the stores
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} has moved to lighter work: mending, minding the stores, keeping the tally. {A_nameDef} grumbles that it's work for an invalid, and does it well.

li.label: Not yet; we need every hand
li.outcome: The council asked {A_nameDef} to keep going a while longer. {A_nameDef} went back to work without arguing, slower than before.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} wants to know why the colony fights the people who come over the hill. Don't they have children too? {A_nameDef} asked it at supper, loudly, while the ones who did the fighting were still eating.\n\nNobody answered, so {A_nameDef} has brought the question to the council.

{A_nameDef} asked the council where the colony came from: not the road or the sky, but before that. Why here? Is it home now, or just where everyone stopped? The grown-ups have given {A_objective} four answers so far, and {A_nameDef} wrote all of them down.
{A_nameDef} wants to know why some people here get rooms of their own and others don't, and whether it's because they're better. {A_nameDef} asked it in front of the people with rooms of their own.
[winter] {A_nameDef} asked why the sun goes away in winter, and whether anyone is sure it will come back. When nobody could explain it to {A_possessive} satisfaction, {A_nameDef} asked the council.
[afterraid] {A_nameDef} watched them bury the raiders yesterday and today asked the council whether the raiders' families know yet, and who will tell them.

li.label: Answer {A_nameDef} straight
li.outcome: The council sat {A_nameDef} down and answered the question as truthfully as it could. {A_nameDef} listened to all of it and then asked six more questions.

li.label: Tell {A_nameDef} a story instead
li.outcome: Instead of an answer, {A_nameDef} got a story: an old one, with a long road in it, a wise animal and a hard lesson at the end. {A_nameDef} has asked to hear it again three times.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {A_nameDef} got the story the old ones tell around the fire, the one about the first winter and the people who walked through it. {A_nameDef} fell asleep before the end and asked for the ending in the morning.

li.label: Ask our most learned to answer it
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} took the question seriously and spent an evening with {A_nameDef}, answering it properly, with a drawing in the dirt. {A_nameDef} went to bed with a head full of it.

outcomes.li: [b:past:scholar] {B_nameDef} answered the question the way a teacher would: with three examples, a diagram, and a question back. {A_nameDef} has been following {B_objective} around since.

li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} answered the question at enormous length, with footnotes. {A_nameDef} fell asleep partway through and has not asked {B_nameDef} anything since.

li.label: That's a question for when you're older
li.outcome: The council told {A_nameDef} it was a question for when {A_pronoun} is older. {A_nameDef} said that's what grown-ups say when they don't know, and went to ask someone else.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} was clearing scrub along the far boundary and found a pack rotted half away, with a journal inside, wrapped in oilcloth and still readable. It belonged to a traveler from {FACTION}. The last entries are about the weather, a sore foot, and somebody waiting at home.\n\nThe council has to decide what to do with it.

[lowtech] Under a fallen tree near the river, {A_nameDef} found old bones, a broken staff and a bundle of bark pages tied with cord, covered in small, careful marks. The marks are {FACTION} writing. Whoever made them was walking somewhere and never got there.

[land:desert] The wind uncovered it: a leather satchel half buried in the sand, and inside, a journal from someone of {FACTION} who crossed this land years ago, or tried to. {A_nameDef} brought it to the council with the sand still in its pages.

[land:tundra|land:boreal] When the snow pulled back this year it left a frozen pack in the open, and inside it a journal. {A_nameDef} thawed the pages by the stove. The writer was from {FACTION}, and the last entry says the cold was getting into the ink.

li.label: Send it home to {FACTION}
li.outcome: The journal went to {FACTION} with the next traveler heading that way, with a note saying where it was found. Word came back that the family had been waiting eleven years to know.

li.label: Read it aloud over supper
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} read the journal aloud over three evenings after supper. The traveler's weather was the colony's weather, the traveler's sore foot was everyone's sore foot, and when it ended the room was quiet for a long time.

li.label: Have our best scholar study it
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} went through the journal page by page and found more than a diary: notes on the land, where the water runs and what grows where, written by someone who had walked all of it. Some of it is already being put to use.

li.label: Bury it with a marker
li.outcome: The colony buried the journal where it was found, under a flat stone with the traveler's name scratched into it. {A_nameDef} goes past it most days on the way to work.

texts.li: The council promised {A_nameDef} something, and the council didn't deliver. {A_nameDef} has stopped pretending not to mind. Today {A_nameDef} stood up at supper and asked, in front of the table, what the council's word is worth.
[trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} isn't angry about the promise the council broke, or says {A_pronoun} isn't. {A_nameDef} just wants to know whether to bother asking next time.

[doubtful|bitter] {A_nameDef} never believed the council's promise in the first place, and now {A_pronoun} has been proved right and is making the most of it. {A_nameDef} wants the council to admit it, out loud.

li.label: Make it up to {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: The council paid {A_nameDef} forty silver from the colony's purse for the trouble. {A_nameDef} counted it twice and put it away, and says the next promise had better be kept.

li.label: Apologize at the table
li.outcome: The council stood up at supper and said, so everyone heard, that it had let {A_nameDef} down. {A_nameDef} didn't say anything. Later {A_pronoun} was seen smiling at the washing-up.

li.label: Have our best talker explain what happened
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} sat down with {A_nameDef} and explained what had come up, what had to come first and why. {A_nameDef} listened to all of it, and said {A_pronoun} understood, mostly.

outcomes.li: [b:office:Speaker] The speaker took {A_nameDef} aside and laid it all out plainly. {A_nameDef} says it's the first time the council has explained itself to {A_objective}, and that it helped.

li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} explained, and explained, and {A_nameDef} heard nothing but excuses. They parted on worse terms than before.

li.label: The council owes nothing for it
li.outcome: The council told {A_nameDef} that promises are made in good faith and sometimes can't be kept, and that's the end of it. {A_nameDef} said {A_pronoun} would remember that.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} pushed the bowl away at supper and said, to nobody in particular, that if {A_pronoun} has to eat the same meal one more time {A_pronoun} will walk to the nearest town for something else. Nobody laughed. Most of the table had been thinking it.\n\n{A_nameDef} has asked the council for something different on the table, even once a week.

[winter] The winter stores are what they are, and the colony has eaten the same thing every day since the first snow. {A_nameDef} has started counting the days out loud at meals, and has asked the council for anything, anything at all, that tastes different.

[trait:Gourmand] {A_nameDef} has written the council a list of eleven meals the colony could be eating instead, with the ingredients for each and where to find them. It is a long list. {A_nameDef} would settle for one.

li.label: Have our best cook try something new each week
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} has taken over one supper a week to try something different. The first was a spiced stew nobody had tasted before, and {A_nameDef} had seconds.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {B_nameDef} roasted roots in the coals with honey and wild thyme for the first of the new suppers. The colony ate it with its fingers and licked them clean.
[b:trait:Gourmand] {B_nameDef} has been waiting a long time for permission. The first of the new suppers had four courses and took all afternoon to cook.

li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} tried something new for supper. It was new. Most of it went back to the kitchen, and {A_nameDef} has stopped complaining about the old meal.

li.label: Send a forager out for something fresh
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} came back from the wild ground with a basket of berries, and the colony ate them out of their hands before supper. It isn't a meal, but it's something different.

outcomes.li: [land:desert] {B_nameDef} came back from the dry country with a sack of cactus fruit, prickles and all. Peeled, they were sweet. The colony ate them all in one sitting.
[land:coast] {B_nameDef} came back from the shore at low tide with a bucket of shellfish and a bag of sea greens. Supper was salty and new.

li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} searched all day and came back with a handful of sour leaves and a bad temper. Supper was the same as always.

riskOutcomes.li: [winter] {B_nameDef} went out into the snow to look for anything fresh and came back hours later with nothing but frozen boots.

li.label: Food is food
li.outcome: The council told {A_nameDef} that food is food and the colony is lucky to have it. {A_nameDef} agreed that the colony is lucky, and then ate the same meal again, slowly.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has done the same job every day for weeks: the same tools, the same corner, the same view of the same wall. Today {A_nameDef} came to the council and asked, politely and with some force, to be given something else to do. Anything else.

[trait:Industrious|trait:HardWorker] {A_nameDef} doesn't mind hard work, and says so. What {A_nameDef} minds is doing the same hard work from dawn to dark, every day, while other people get to do different hard work. {A_nameDef} wants a turn at something new.
{A_nameDef} was found this morning staring at {A_possessive} workbench as if it had insulted {A_objective}. "Something else," {A_nameDef} told the council later. "For a week. A day. I'm not fussy."

li.label: Give {A_nameDef} a week of something different
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} has a week away from the old job, doing whatever needs doing elsewhere. {A_nameDef} is worse at all of it and visibly happier.

li.label: Have someone teach {A_nameDef} a new trade
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} has taken {A_nameDef} on as a student in {B_possessive} own trade. {A_nameDef} is clumsy at it, asks a great many questions and looks forward to every lesson.

li.reason: Needs someone with a trade to teach

li.label: Rotate everyone's chores once a week
li.outcome: The council has put the chores on a rotation: once a week, everyone does someone else's job. Nobody does it as well, and everyone has something new to complain about.

li.label: Someone has to do it
li.outcome: The council told {A_nameDef} that someone has to do the work, and {A_nameDef} does it best. {A_nameDef} went back to the same corner and the same wall.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} sleeps in a room with too many other people, eats at a table with too many elbows, and has started taking {A_possessive} meals outside to get some air. {A_nameDef} wants the council to do something about the crowding.

[winter] Winter has driven everyone indoors, and indoors isn't big enough. {A_nameDef} was elbowed off the end of the bench at supper for the third time this week and came straight to the council, still holding {A_possessive} bowl.

[trait:Abrasive] {A_nameDef} has told several people, at volume, that there are too many of them in too little room, and that {A_pronoun} would like some of them elsewhere. The council has been asked to settle it before {A_nameDef} settles it.

li.label: Give {A_nameDef} a corner of the storeroom
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} has a cot behind a curtain in the corner of the storeroom, among the sacks and the barrels. It smells of onions. It's {A_possessive} own.

li.label: Supper in two sittings
li.outcome: Supper now comes in two sittings, early and late, and there's room on the bench for everyone's elbows. The cook works longer. Everyone else is grateful.

li.label: Have a builder mark out a new room
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} walked the ground with {A_nameDef} and drove stakes in where a new room could go, with string between them. It will take materials and hands to build. For now, {A_nameDef} goes and stands in it some evenings.

li.label: the walk round the new room
Everyone is crowded
li.outcome: The council told {A_nameDef} that everyone is crowded and {A_nameDef} will have to put up with it like everyone else. {A_nameDef} went back to eating outside.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has been hanging around {B_nameDef}'s workbench every day, handing over tools before {B_nameDef} asks for them. Today {A_nameDef} asked to make something real, with real tools, start to finish.\n\n{B_nameDef} said to ask the council.

{A_nameDef} took apart a broken chair this morning to see how it was made, and put most of it back together again. {B_nameDef} found the leftover pieces and the proud look, and came to the council to ask what to do with {A_objective}.

[lowtech] {A_nameDef} has been watching {B_nameDef} work at the bench for weeks, and today brought {B_objective} a spoon {A_pronoun} had carved on {A_possessive} own with a borrowed knife. It's crooked. It holds soup. {A_nameDef} wants to learn properly.

li.label: {B_nameDef} takes {A_nameDef} on as an apprentice
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is {B_nameDef}'s apprentice now, with a stool at the end of the bench and a set of small tools. The first lesson was how to sweep up. The second was how to hold a chisel, and {A_nameDef} is still talking about it.

li.label: Small jobs only, under {B_nameDef}'s eye
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} can help at the bench with small jobs, as long as {B_nameDef} is watching. Sanding, sorting nails, holding things steady. {A_nameDef} says it's not real work, and does every bit of it.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} make one thing, start to finish
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} made a stool, start to finish, with {B_nameDef} sitting on {B_possessive} hands nearby. It wobbles. {A_nameDef} sits on it at every meal.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} made a stool, start to finish, and it came apart the first time anyone sat on it. {B_nameDef} told {A_objective} that everybody's first one does, and showed {A_objective} the remains of {B_possessive} own.

li.label: Play is a child's work
li.outcome: The council told {A_nameDef} there's time enough for work when {A_pronoun} is grown, and sent {A_objective} off to play. {A_nameDef} went, and played at being a carpenter.

texts.li: {B_nameDef} has been up three nights running with {A_nameDef}, who has {ILLNESS}, and it shows: this morning {B_nameDef} fell asleep sitting up at breakfast with the spoon in {B_possessive} hand. {A_nameDef} is no better and no worse. {B_nameDef} says {B_pronoun} can manage another night.

{B_nameDef} has been tending {A_nameDef}'s {ILLNESS} day and night, and this afternoon mixed up two jars on the shelf and had to start the dressing again. Nothing came of it. {B_nameDef} has asked the council to stop looking at {B_objective} like that.

li.label: {B_nameDef} sleeps; someone else sits up
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} was sent to bed and slept fourteen hours. Someone else sat up with {A_nameDef}, following {B_nameDef}'s written instructions to the letter, and woke {B_objective} only once.

li.reason: Needs someone else who knows some doctoring (Medicine 2 or more)

li.label: {B_nameDef} keeps watch; others cover {B_possessive} work
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} stays at {A_nameDef}'s bedside, and the others are covering {B_possessive} other work. {A_nameDef} is starting to mend. {B_nameDef} looks like a ghost.

li.label: Teach the basics to everyone who's awake
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} spent an evening teaching anyone awake how to take a fever, change a dressing and know when to come and get {B_objective}. Now there are three people sitting with {A_nameDef} in turns, and {B_nameDef} sleeps between.
